topic: how the chain enters a forecast
decision: final = guide-anchored benchmark + weight x (chain forecast - benchmark) + events propagated through the graph; every term of the chain forecast maps to one of the brief's decisions (lag kernel, mechanism multiplier, attribution share, regime)
alternatives_considered: Replace the guide with the chain; keep the chain as a side cross-check (the previous design)
reason: Analyst review 2026-09-26: the forecasts must be built from the analysis, logic before regression. The back-test decides how much the chain counts, so the structure is explicit and the weight is evidence, not taste
effect: Each print has a term table on the dashboard, in model_report.md and in the note

topic: weight rule (Nordic)
decision: Weight = encompassing beta of (actual - guide) on the chain's tilt over the walk-forward quarters if t >= 2, capped to [0, 1]; else 0. If several chain models pass, the lower walk-forward RMSE wins
alternatives_considered: Inverse-MSE weights; fixed judgmental weight; a mechanism prior (booked share of orders)
reason: The encompassing regression is the forecast-combination weight (Fair-Shiller); the t-bar keeps a noisy beta from entering. Fixed in config before the live numbers
effect: h=1: CH beta -0.66 (t -2.1), GR -0.05 -> weight 0. h=2: CH +3.2 (t 2.6), GR +1.3 (t 3.6) -> GR, weight 1 (the Q4 line)

topic: chain as reasoned (CH)
decision: Nordic tilt = share_t x [revenue_(t-4) x (1 + m x kernel-weighted sell-out YoY) - guide_t]; nothing fitted
alternatives_considered: GR only (one fitted slope hides attribution and mechanism in one coefficient)
reason: Logic first: each coefficient is a decision with its own evidence; the back-test then says whether the logic holds
effect: h=1 no information (the chain only speaks for the ~17% slice, and its disagreement is about mix); h=2 right direction, slope ~3: Nordic moves ~3x the slice (common cycle across its consumer customers)

topic: why the guide wins the guided quarter
decision: Explain h=1 by mechanism, not only by the score: Nordic guides from orders in hand; the graph kernel puts Q3's driving demand at lags 1-2 (mean 1.4 q) and component lead times are 12-16 weeks, so the demand that sets Q3 was ordered before the 6 Aug guide
alternatives_considered: Report the score alone
reason: The lag decision predicts the back-test result; that is the link between the lag question and the forecast
effect: The note states the lag structure as the reason the guided quarter is anchored on the guide and the chain is used one quarter out

topic: one model of the guide error for all three forecasts
decision: Expected guide error = company habit alpha (partially pooled: mu, tau^2 from the 12 peers' quarterly guides by DerSimonian-Laird; own errors shrunk by tau^2/(tau^2+s^2/n)) + gamma x BUILDING state of quarter t-1 (step 3b cycle_state, known at the forecast date; peers, company fixed effects, SE clustered by quarter, used if |t| >= 2). Point = guide mid x (1 + expected error) + chain terms (7c); range = predictive sd. Replaces the regime-dated beats (F14), the GN year filter (F15) and the extra_uncertainty lines
alternatives_considered: Keep per-company rules (regime beats, year filters); full Bayesian hierarchical model; four state dummies; z-score of distributor days as a continuous state
reason: Analyst request 2026-09-27: one clean, logical rule instead of patches. The beat is management's forecast error (K1); a company's habit is estimated best with its peers when it has few guides; the only channel information that can beat a guide is news after it was set, i.e. the state of the channel the supply-chain analysis measures. One contrast (building) had an economic prior; thresholds of cycle_state were set after seeing 2020-26 (D22, disclosed); robustness: state lagged 2 quarters
effect: gamma -1.25 pts (t -3.2, 621 firm-quarters; lag 2: -1.66, t -4.5); peers' habit +1.9%, spread 0.5 pts: own records weigh 20% (Nordic, n 21) and 11% (Logitech, n 5). Nordic 237.4 -> 233.5 (220-247), Logitech 1243.7 -> 1247.0 (1196-1298), GN 2236 -> 2202. Nordic walk-forward (n 14): 5.2 pts vs 5.4 for the past-4 beat and 5.6 for the guide midpoint

Ranges from out-of-sample errors; the hand-set gm_point / gm_range / ebita_adj_margin_* keys are removed

reason: The brief checklist flagged the three margins as the only forecasts not derived from data; Logitech beat its call GM guide in all 4 quarters (+0.6 to +2.3 pts)

topic: Nordic GM: pre-registered channel-excess term; one-off-adjusted GM series
decision: Pre-registered before estimation (config guidance_anchor.margins.nordic_excess, written as 'F19' and relabelled F25 because F19 was taken; specification unchanged): dGM_it = firm effect + delta x excess_t-1, excess = step 3b cycle state building or drawdown in t-1 (Microchip distributor days, common to all firms), delta on the 12 peers (Pipeline D XBRL revenue and COGS, GM = 1 - COGS / revenue, consecutive quarters only), |dGM| > 10 pts dropped as accounting events, SE clustered by quarter (CR1). Adopt only if delta < 0 with |t| >= 2 AND 'last quarter + delta_t x excess_t-1' beats 'last quarter' walk-forward on Nordic (delta_t from peer rows dated <= t-1). Result: delta -0.24 pts (se 0.22, t -1.11; n 674 firm-quarters, 64 quarters 2010Q4-2026Q3, 27 excess quarters, 18 accounting events dropped). Not adopted: fails the t bar, and the walk-forward does not improve (RMSE 2.35 with the term vs 2.34 without, n 21 Nordic targets 2021Q2-2026Q2, 10 of them after an excess quarter). The term stays as a scenario (gm_if_excess = point + delta = 52.9%). Also: nordic_gm() now uses the one-off-adjusted GM (panel nordic_gm_adj: Q2 2024 write-down 42.0 -> 49.8, Q4 2025 one-off 54.9 -> 52.0), P116
alternatives_considered: Building-only or drawdown-only states, excluding Microchip (the state's own source), keeping the >10 pt moves: all computed and shown as labelled diagnostics in margin_excess_effect.csv, none used for adoption (they would be post-hoc choices); a state-dependent Nordic-only estimate (21 quarters, one cycle: no power)
reason: Mechanism (price protection / ASP concessions when the channel is long) is plausible, so it was specified and tested before being allowed to move a number; the peers give the power Nordic's 21 quarters lack. The adoption bar is the one used elsewhere (t >= 2) plus an out-of-sample gain on Nordic itself
effect: Excess term: no change (not adopted; state 2026Q2 = lean, so it would add 0 even if adopted). One-off fix: Nordic Q3 GM point 53.1% unchanged (base 2026Q2 has no one-off); walk-forward RMSE of 'last quarter' 3.2 -> 2.1 pts (4q mean 3.6 -> 2.6, same quarter LY 5.5 -> 4.3); normal-regime sd 3.55 -> 0.92 pts; 80% range 48.6-57.6 -> 51.9-54.3%. Microchip -0.15 (t -0.70); building only -0.42 (t -1.51); drawdown only +0.06 (t 0.27)

topic: Nordic Q4 point model: GRi (Logitech sell-in through the Nordic -> ODM -> Logitech segment)
decision: Q4 (h=2) point = GRi: Nordic consumer YoY = a + b x (sum_k w_k x Logitech SELL-IN YoY_t-k), kernel w only over the graph segment from Nordic to Logitech (stop_at='logitech': 90% lag 1, 10% lag 2); the unreported Logitech quarter = our bias-corrected sell-in forecast (guide mid x (1 + mean past beat)), switch forecast_next_quarter.gri_fill. GR (sell-through proxy through the whole graph, persistence) stays logged as a challenger; supersedes F24's point model

reason: Economic: Nordic's orders follow what Logitech builds and ships (sell-in = sell-through + channel change, the bullwhip reaches Nordic through that), not what consumers buy; driving by sell-in removes the retail / distributor edges and the sell-through-gap guess. Analyst decision 2026-09-27 (session 683fda): 'GRi as the Q4 point model' Fill (analyst 2026-09-27, session 683fda: 'use our forecast'): the fill replaces a number nobody has yet - Logitech's unreported quarter - and Logitech has already told us what it plans to ship. Its guide missed from the same side every time (+0.5 to +2.1%), so guide x (1 + mean past beat) tracked the outcome within 1.5 pts in every quarter after the first (errors -2.1, +0.4, -0.1, +1.4, -0.6; RMSE 1.17 vs 2.61 for persistence). For 2026Q3 the two fills disagree by the most in the sample: the bias-corrected guide says sell-in slows to +3.0% (the guide carries ~USD 20m of supplier-incident loss), persistence says +6.9%; carrying last quarter forward would ignore a slowdown the company has announced. The 5-quarter test cannot confirm it statistically (DM t -1.0; 99% of the gain from 2025Q2, the first guide, with no history to correct), so the choice rests on this reasoning and is scored at the Feb 2027 print; persistence stays one config line away (218.6)
effect: h=2 walk-forward revenue RMSE GRi 25.4 vs GR 28.0 (n 9; 0.54x vs 0.59x the benchmark) - post-hoc and within noise (expected MSE gain of a better input ~6%). Fill: our sell-in forecast errs 1.17 vs 2.61 for persistence (5 quarters) but fails F24's bar (DM t -1.0, 99% of the gain from 2025Q2); persistence fill gives Q4 218.6 and h=2 RMSE 24.7. Q4 2026: GRi 208.9 (176-242) vs GR 222.4

Logitech: guide set at the guide-date rates (USD = cc 0-3% for Q2 FY27, assumed 0); the term is applied only if guide + term beats the guide walk-forward. Nordic: USD throughout, no term. Margins (F18 branch stated in each rule): a point guide -> guide + mean past error; only a floor -> the walk-forward winner; the same race is run for Logitech and Nordic and reported
alternatives_considered: Keep GN's carried-forward -1.5; apply the Logitech FX term regardless; FRED rates (timed out; the ECB is the primary publisher)
reason: Analyst review 2026-09-27: GN had an explicit hand FX line while Logitech and Nordic had none, and the margin rules differed by company without a stated reason
effect: GN Q3 FX +1.47 pts (USD +1.6% vs DKK YoY) instead of -1.5: revenue about +3% (~ +65 DKKm).
